notes:
Top-level: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood hosted API first; now moving to Dedicated POC.

Key contacts: CTO Elena Marquez (technical owner), Head of Product Marcus Lee, AE Jordan Hayes, SE Priya Raman, Infra lead Tom Kline. CSM assigned for onboarding: Liam Ortega.

Use-case detail: primary workload is customer support assistant (multi-turn, context window ~8k), secondary is embeddings for document search + reranker for result ordering. Expected steady-state: 150-250 QPS for embeddings queries during peak; support assistant ~60 concurrent sessions.

Performance & SLOs: target p95 generation latency <= 450ms for short-turn responses (<150 tokens). Throughput target for embeddings path: 200 QPS with <120ms median. Cost sensitivity: mid-high; want 25-40% cost savings vs current managed provider.

Model preferences: prefer open/Redwood-verified family (13B quantized candidate), fallback to smaller 7B variant for bursty traffic. Interested in quantization profiles and kernel-level tuning.

Dedicated POC plan (agreed): 2-week sandbox Dedicated cluster in NA region, canary rollout plan: start with 5% traffic to Dedicated variant (routing by user segment) -> monitor 48h -> increase to 25% -> 2x24h stable -> full cutover. Canary metrics: p95 latency, error rate, token cost delta, model output-quality via sample prompt set.

Fallback & routing strategy: primary route to Dedicated (13B quantized). Fallback chain: Dedicated 13B -> Dedicated 7B quantized -> Hosted compatible 13B (cross-region) -> Hosted smallest variant. Region failover: NA primary, EU warm standby — policy to failover on region-wide outage or sustained latency degradation (>30% p95 increase for >10 minutes).

Rollback triggers: sustained error rate >2% OR p95 latency >800ms OR token cost >+30% vs baseline OR automated QA degradation on eval prompt set (drop in ROUGE/EM-like metrics). Rollback window target: full rollback within 15 minutes via routing policy.

Operational asks: need route-level observability in Console (per-model p95, token breakdown), tracing hooks to associate requests to sessions, and ability to pin specific model version for select tenants. Requesting evaluation access to Optimize recommendations for batching/caching.

Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, audit logs for request payload metadata (no PII in logs), KMS integration for workspace keys, and EU data residency option for EU customers. Legal working on DPA; infra requires VPC peering and egress rules.

POC success criteria (customer-defined): 1) meet p95 latency target under target load, 2) <=1.5% error rate, 3) token cost within budgeted envelope (<= planned ARR scenario), 4) smooth canary to full cutover with no regressions in quality on eval set.

Next steps (short): SE to share Dedicated sizing worksheet + SOW draft by 2026-03-12. Infra to provision VPC peering window 2026-03-18. Legal to complete DPA redlines by 2026-04-01. AE to secure procurement kickoff date.

Direct quote: CTO Elena — "we need predictable economics and a clear rollback path; if you can demonstrate stable p95 and cost benefits in the POC, we can move to a 12mo commit."
